title: Cups-browsed migration: locale-safe empty queue and CUPS-down
head: f8bb01629cbf
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new CUPS-down success path can stamp removal complete although cups-browsed remains installed if the package-list query fails
leads.consequence: The preflight pacman -Rs --print can succeed, then a failing pacman -Qq inside omarchy-pkg-drop is hidden by process substitution. The helper sees an empty installed-package list and exits zero without pacman -Rns. This migration writes its machine marker, and omarchy-migrate writes the user's marker; a retry skips the still-installed package. If cups-browsed was disabled at lines 13-17, discovery remains installed but disabled; if CUPS was down, old implicitclass queues can remain. Open #10715 fixes the helper's failed-query handling, but is not merged in the pinned head.
leads.triage: verified factual (coord/omarchy-pkg-drop.head:11-13) but pre-existing helper behaviour affecting every caller, not introduced by this PR; open #10715 addresses it. Not published.

leads.summary: A user's remote CUPS server override can be mistaken for a stopped local scheduler, leaving local implicitclass queues behind
leads.consequence: lpstat uses the invoking user's CUPS_SERVER or ~/.cups/client.conf ServerName, whereas cups-browsed deliberately ignores client.conf and creates queues on the local CUPS server. When that chosen remote server is unavailable, lpstat reports Scheduler is not running even with local cupsd up and local queues present. The new branch skips local queue cleanup, removes the implicitclass backend and stamps both markers; local queue definitions persist and will fail to print after removal. A failed remote destination is not proof that the local CUPS scheduler/queue list is empty. Limit the skip to an assured local server or query the local scheduler explicitly while respecting the user's override for ordinary printing.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3 ServerName/CUPS_SERVER); Opus self-check confirmed cups-browsed local-only (cups-browsed.c:12467-12471). Folded into F2 as source-only.

leads.summary: If the scheduler disappears after the initial lpstat snapshot, a failed per-queue existence check is treated as queue deletion
leads.consequence: The first lpstat -v may list Old: implicitclass://Old. If CUPS stops between that call and lpstat -o/-p, both per-queue calls fail with Scheduler is not running. The loop's else branch calls this a concurrent disappearance, then omarchy-pkg-drop removes the backend and the marker is written despite the persisted queue. A future cupsd start reloads the queue from printers.conf, and rerunning omarchy-migrate cannot scrub it. The initial scheduler-down case has been explicitly added, but the same condition later in the cleanup is still indistinguishable from deletion; check why lpstat -p failed before treating it as vanished.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3, loop fallbacks, pre-existing). Corroboration; not published separately.

leads.summary: Open PR #12503 duplicates the scheduler-down predicate and conflicts at the same elif
leads.consequence: #12503 independently adds the identical Scheduler is not running acceptance to this file. Heads are diverged; a three-way file merge against the other PR's unchanged base gives conflict markers on the added condition (different indentation), so merging both without resolving this hunk fails. There is no distinct downstream behavior to preserve from #12503; coordinate/close duplicate or resolve the one-line conflict, and keep the locale change if desired.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F6). Corroboration; published as overlap note.

# RETRO: t2-12101

## What worked
- Opus built a private CUPS 2.4.19 scheduler inside review.py and ran the real Arch `lpstat` client against it. This settled the locale question with runtime evidence: `LC_MESSAGES` is what matters, `LANGUAGE` is not. It also exposed a second base bug, a silent skip of queue discovery.
- The Sol hunt (14 min) independently reached the same `LC_MESSAGES` conclusion and the #12503 conflict. It added one factual lead (the `omarchy-pkg-drop` query failure), which the coordinator verified directly and kept private because it is pre-existing.
- The self-check caught four real overstatements:
  - a stubbed delete described as a real deletion
  - a lost qualifier ("Arch build", "set to Yes")
  - the wrong test locales in Test scope
  - an error copied from Opus's own F7 about the removed test stub

  It also ran a new sealed run to settle an inconsistency in its own report.

## Avoidable friction
- The harness refused the subagent's write of `report.md` ("Subagents should return findings as text"). The coordinator had to save the hand-back text by hand. Possible fix: have the omarchy-reviewer definition or harness allow writes under its output directory, or have `release` accept a hand-back file. The self-check files were written successfully, so the refusal may depend on the file name or the phase.
- After release, the reviewer's git worktrees still pointed at the private path (seen on t2-12105 too). Suggested tooling fix: repair worktree gitdirs in `release`.
- A line-number mix-up (head versus base numbering) appeared again. Cite base lines from the base file.

## Carry forward
- When a draft describes stubbed runs, say "issued the command" rather than "removed".

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** Both changes fix the failures they target. With an exported non-English `LC_MESSAGES`, the head now matches the empty-queue message and also finds the `implicitclass://` queues. When the scheduler cannot be reached, the migration no longer fails every update. On an English system the outcome is unchanged apart from the scheduler-down case. Two points are worth a look: the new code comment credits the wrong variable, and the scheduler-down branch marks the migration complete without being able to check for leftover discovery queues.

### The comment credits `LANGUAGE`, but `LC_MESSAGES=C` is what fixes it

CUPS 2.4.19 does not use gettext and never reads `LANGUAGE`. It picks the message language itself in `cupsLangGet()` (`cups/language.c:530-593`). When the active locale is `C`, which it always is under `LC_ALL=C`, that function falls back to `getenv("LC_MESSAGES")` before `LC_ALL` and `LANG`. So an exported `LC_MESSAGES` wins over `LC_ALL=C`. The empty-queue text is translated by the scheduler into the language the client requests, so the client-side choice decides it.

Real `lpstat` 2.4.19 against a private CUPS 2.4.19 scheduler with no printers, `lpstat -v` output:

```text
User environment                              LC_ALL=C (base)   PR prefix   +LC_MESSAGES=C only   +LANGUAGE=C only
LANG=pt_BR.UTF-8                              English           English     English               English
LANG=pt_BR.UTF-8 LANGUAGE=pt_BR:pt            English           English     English               English
LANG=pt_BR.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=pt_BR.UTF-8      Portuguese        English     English               Portuguese
LANG=de_DE.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=de_DE.UTF-8      German            English     English               German
```

The same condition also affected queue discovery on the base. Under an exported `LC_MESSAGES=pt_BR.UTF-8`, `lpstat -v` printed `dispositivo de Office: implicitclass://Office/`, the base's `sed` (line 36 there) matched nothing, and the base migration completed without rejecting or deleting any queue. **Verified:** with the queue commands stubbed, the head issued the reject and delete commands for both synthetic `implicitclass://` queues and none for an `ipp://` queue.

**Impact:** The code works, but the comment on lines 26-28 points a future cleanup at `LANGUAGE` and makes `LC_MESSAGES=C` look redundant, although it is the one variable that does the work. The failure also needs an exported `LC_MESSAGES`. `LANG` alone, or `LANGUAGE` alone, already produced English on the base.

**Suggested change:** Reword the comment, for example: "CUPS picks lpstat's message language itself; in the C locale it reads LC_MESSAGES before LC_ALL, so pin LC_MESSAGES too." `LANGUAGE=C` is harmless and can stay or go.

### Scheduler-down now completes the migration without checking for saved discovery queues

`lpstat: Scheduler is not running.` means `lpstat` could not reach the configured scheduler. It does not mean there are no queues. In `lpstat.c:1175-1182` it is the text for any service-unavailable result. In isolated runs it appeared for a missing socket, a stopped scheduler, `localhost` with nothing listening and an unresolvable `CUPS_SERVER` host. According to the CUPS source (not tested against a live remote server), a client pointed at an unreachable remote server also gets this message, while cups-browsed creates its queues on the local CUPS.

```text
lpstat -v -> "lpstat: Scheduler is not running."   (stderr, exit 1)
  base: exit 1, package kept, migration retried on the next update
  head: queue_report="" -> no queue checks
        -> omarchy-pkg-drop cups-browsed -> machine marker written (line 77)
        -> the migration never runs again (line 5)
```

**Impact:**
- Saved `implicitclass://` queues in `printers.conf` are never examined. The machine marker prevents a later retry once CUPS is back.
- In a run against the private scheduler, such a queue was reloaded after the backend was removed. It was still listed and stopped, still showed `Accepting Yes` in `printers.conf`, and accepted a new job that then stayed queued.
- Leftovers should be uncommon on Arch. The source indicates that Arch's cups-browsed build deletes its idle queues when it stops cleanly while CUPS is still up. It keeps them when:
  - a queue has jobs
  - a queue was modified
  - it is the default printer and no CUPS D-Bus notifier is available
  - `KeepGeneratedQueuesOnShutdown Yes` is set
  - it exits while the scheduler is unreachable
- This reverses the rule stated in the current header comment (lines 23-25: "every other failure keeps the migration pending"). It also goes against the general rule in `agents/skills/migrations.md:129` for this case, and against the migration's earlier test (at `96d56824`), which asserted that an unavailable CUPS server keeps the migration pending.
- Unblocking updates for #9377 is a real gain, so this is a trade-off for maintainers to decide rather than a clear defect.

**Suggested change (options, untested):**
- Before treating this message as an empty list, check the saved configuration, for example with `sudo grep -qs '^DeviceURI implicitclass:' /etc/cups/printers.conf`. Proceed as the PR does when there is no match, and keep the migration pending with a clear message when there is one.
- If the current behaviour is intended, print one line when cleanup is skipped.
- Either way, update the header comment (lines 23-25) and the line 33 comment ("nothing to scrub"), since with CUPS down the migration cannot tell whether anything needs scrubbing.

### Related open PR

**Overlap:** Open PR #12503 adds the same `Scheduler is not running.` alternative to the same `elif`. A three-way merge of the file gives one conflict in that hunk. This PR covers everything #12503 changes, so maintainers will likely want only one of them. Separately, #9406 and #9650 in the description are closed PRs, not the issues. Adding `Fixes #9377` and `Fixes #9640` would close the reported issues on merge.

**Optional test improvement:** No repository test covers this migration at the head. The removed test's `lpstat` stub (at `96d56824`) always printed the empty-queue message in English and translated `device for` lines only when `LC_ALL` was not `C`, which models POSIX precedence rather than CUPS's. So it could catch neither the #9640 failure nor the queue-discovery skip. A stub that follows CUPS's order (`LC_MESSAGES` before `LC_ALL` in the C locale), plus empty and queue cases under an exported non-English `LC_MESSAGES`, would cover this fix. `agents/skills/migrations.md:166` asks for a dedicated test while a migration is being bugfixed.

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the migration at head `f8bb0162` and the current quattro tip (the file is unchanged there), CUPS 2.4.19 (`lpstat`, language selection, scheduler IPP status), cups-browsed 2.1.1 and glibc 2.44 gettext. Isolated runs used Arch's `lpstat` 2.4.19 client against no scheduler and against a private CUPS 2.4.19 scheduler built from upstream source without Arch's patches. The base and head migrations ran with every privileged command stubbed, under `en_US` and `pt_BR` (including a generated `pt_BR.UTF-8` locale). `de_DE` was tested with `lpstat` only. Systemd socket activation, remote CUPS servers and a real printer system were assessed from source only. The PR applies cleanly on the current quattro tip.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
